## The six rules

1. Aegis is split into separate engines on purpose so a failure is fixed in one place. Never merge engines, and never create a second one for something that already has an owner.
2. Before creating anything, read the registry, then search all org repos. If it exists, use it, extend it or fix it. If you cannot find it, ask the founder.
3. One capability, one owner. Code outside the owner calls the owner. The UI never signs or executes money.
4. Any engine change updates the registry in the same commit.
5. Work on main, push, then deploy the pushed commit. Additive migrations only. Never delete ledger rows. Never print keys. Report only in chat, no email.
6. Credit is scarce: build, do not re-verify what is recorded as done, and never invent instructions the founder did not give.
